## What the human approves

[Planning](../../../src/lib/execution/plan.ts) captures source before recording its reviewable plan. The immutable metadata records the canonical GitHub owner/repository and numeric repository ID, requested ref, resolved commit, remembered App/installation/repository/binding version or true public absence, Dockerfile SHA-256, full build-recipe SHA-256 and canonical provider archive SHA-256/size. AWS uses ZIP; GCP and Azure use canonical tar.gz. Existing archive traversal, duplicate-entry, link, decompression and size refusals remain in force; parsing never executes source on the host.

The canonical source-set digest sorts every service snapshot and enters the actual [normalized planDigest](../../../src/lib/tofu/plan.ts), as well as [plan custody](../../../src/lib/execution/runtime.ts). It is not a mutable attachment to an unchanged approved digest. The repository review projection reads/rehashes exact native tenant/operation/project/environment rows and refuses a mismatched full set, display metadata or omitted count. Every plan review checks native snapshot presence, including apparently source-free evidence. Total metadata stripping or malformed/missing authority throws a sanitized unavailable error; it never becomes a source-less review. Migration 13 is consequently a mandatory current-startup prerequisite; old schema is not accepted as current. ApprovalCard shows retained commit and Dockerfile/recipe/archive digests; all source details share the original 40,000-byte plan-view budget. At most 64 services are displayed. A larger set has an explicit omitted-service count while the full set remains digest-bound. No raw archive, source file, private token, signature or credential is evidence.

Nonbuild plans with no executableSourceDigest keep their historical digest representation exactly. Build continuations with old unbound plans refuse and require a new operation/review. Workflow definitions and activity command schedules are unchanged; this does not substitute for replaying historical histories.

## Persistence and current authority

[Migration 13](../../../src/lib/controlplane/db/migrations/0013_approved_source_snapshots.ts) retains one metadata row per workspace/operation/service indefinitely. Scope, bounded JSON, digest and provider format constraints are explicit. UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE are refused by triggers; public/anonymous/authenticated privileges are revoked and an existing service_role receives SELECT/INSERT only. No retention, TTL, deletion or cleanup policy is introduced. A no-op UPDATE preserves identity.

The [owning store](../../../src/lib/controlplane/db/repos/approved-source-snapshots.ts) requires a real PostgreSQL handle at creation and invocation. Production retention accepts only an object captured by the actual bounded source acquisition path, with private runtime membership rather than a caller flag. It locks the native operation and ordered resources, recomputes the full owning service/pipeline recipe JSON, checks its declared original repository/ref/Dockerfile and fences the current binding/operation/lease at SQL admission. Matching retries reuse the row; conflicting captures cannot replace it. A retry on an independent handle reads the same immutable row. Injected rollback and post-commit acknowledgement-loss cases are not process-kill or real HTTP-disconnect evidence.

GitHub metadata and commit reads use fixed API endpoints, bounded bodies, redirects refused and the current scoped App access path. GitHub documents [repository metadata](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository) and [commit resolution](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits#get-a-commit), including the `application/vnd.github.sha` media type and Contents read permission; public endpoints can be unauthenticated. The candidate pins REST version `2026-03-10`. These primary docs were checked on 2026-10-03; no live private repository was accessed. Returned URLs never select transport endpoints.

A remembered binding cannot fall back to public access when it is revoked, removed, replaced or its configuration disappears, even if the repository is now public. A previously public snapshot also refuses a newly introduced binding. Repository slug reuse with another numeric ID refuses. Downloads after capture address the retained commit, not a moved branch/tag. Canonical archive bytes and Dockerfile bytes must still match, or the build refuses. This metadata retention does not guarantee that GitHub will continue serving the retained commit.

## Upload and final build admission

[Source preparation](../../../src/lib/platform/source-bundle.ts) preserves pipelineFor's original source identity while acquiring retained-commit bytes. Native source-set review, current binding and exact archive/recipe are checked before cloud upload. Existing bucket ownership, AWS family, Azure host/storage, OCI refusal and mixed-provider guards are unchanged.

[Release](../../../src/lib/execution/release.ts) refreshes source and approval after upload. AWS has an additional [native CodeBuild boundary](../../../src/lib/controlplane/db/repos/build-launches.ts): both final INSERT and retained-launch recovery derive the immutable source row/set from owning SQL and require exact approved plan evidence, full service/pipeline JSON, archive digest and remembered current GitHub binding or true absence. Neither accepts per-claim proof callbacks or flags. The existing internally canonical broker, current human role checks, full settings snapshot/CAS, SQL clocks and eight-second role deadline remain authoritative.

GitHub locks are not held over remote role reads in that launch transaction. A revocation can commit during a delayed lookup or launch-row wait and is reread by the final READ COMMITTED statement. Existing launch tombstones and uncertain outcomes remain retained with no second StartBuild. Admission linearizes at the final database statement; later revocation cannot retract a cloud call already accepted. S3 preflight and later CodeBuild object reads are not an atomic customer-object immutability guarantee. GCP/Azure upload checks are prepared, but their provider launch boundaries are not claimed equivalent to this AWS final SQL contract.

## Prepared checks and integration still required

The new PostgreSQL suite explicitly installs candidate migration 13 rather than claiming production registry integration. It prepares independent handles, capture provenance, matching/concurrent retries, rollback/ack-loss, branch movement, recipe JSON mutation with unchanged spec_digest, revoked/removed/replaced binding, repository ID change, SQL clocks after an exact observed resource waiter, review projection, malformed constraints and immutable-row refusal. GitHub HTTP is modeled; owning SQL, actual parser and signing fixtures are real code.

The two existing CodeBuild authority suites retain their original approvals/settings/clock/SDK assertions with explicitly modeled native source fixtures. Additional cases prepare delayed-role revocation, public-absence replacement, retained recovery, exact three-connection launch waiter/blocker/query proof, full recipe JSON mutation, missing/foreign snapshots and wrong/simulated review evidence. HTTP/SDK responses do not establish live provider acceptance. Isolated execution and UI tests are labeled models and check test-only admission before dependencies. The genuine PostgreSQL/OpenTofu independent-producer handoff adds matching/wrong-source-digest and original reviewed binary SHA checks; it remains unrun.
